clue.text: Special fare you may get if you're patient

definitions.text: Special fare you may get if you're patient

parts.words: Special fare you may get if you're patient
parts.note: a patient here is someone in hospital, and the fare is the restricted food prescribed for the sick

explanation.surface: A passenger hoping for a discounted ticket if they are willing to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' and 'patient' suggest a traveller waiting calmly for a cheap ticket; the fare is food and the patient is someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Food prescribed for someone in a sickbed is a restricted regime of meals.

clue.text: Set on returning valuable pieces of paper

indicators.note: in a down clue returning means the words set on are read from the bottom back to the top

explanation.surface: Someone sets about recovering some precious documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper money, slips of paper carrying value.

clue.text: Modified form of treadle

indicators.note: a new form of the word treadle means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reshaped version of the foot pedal on an old sewing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modified has been changed.

clue.text: I ring a girl up for a healing tincture

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the girl's name is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone phones a girlfriend to ask for some antiseptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the letter O; 'up' turns ENID into DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic solution of this element is a classic antiseptic dabbed on cuts.

clue.text: is held up by storehouses making initial payments

indicators.note: held by the storehouses means the small word is kept inside them

parts.note: depots are storehouses

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is is written upwards as SI

explanation.surface: Something is propped up by warehouses that are handing over first instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is held up' reads as something propped up; in a down clue 'up' reverses, and 'making' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Down payments made at the start of a purchase secure the goods.

clue.text: Could it make me a lord? Yes!

definitions.text: Could it make me a lord? Yes!

indicators.note: asking what the letters could make signals that me a lord are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hopeful commoner asks whether something could ennoble them, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of ME A LORD rearrange to the title that would make one a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl's rank or territory is a peerage that would make its holder a lord.

clue.text: Fashionable material for children to play with

definitions.text: Fashionable material for children to play with

parts.words: Fashionable material for children to play with
parts.note: the material is fashionable in the sense that it is used for fashioning or shaping things, a soft stuff children mould

explanation.surface: A trendy fabric sold for children's games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' suggests trendy; it really means able to be fashioned, or shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasticine-like modelling stuff is a soft pliable substance children shape.

clue.text: Falling for a display of acrobatics

explanation.surface: A gymnast comes off the beam during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling is toppling over and over, and acrobats' somersaults and handsprings are this act too.

clue.text: Essential equipment for a sempstress who isn't allowed to use her imagination?

definitions.text: Essential equipment for a sempstress who isn't allowed to use her imagination?

parts.words: Essential equipment for a sempstress who isn't allowed to use her imagination?
parts.note: a seamstress forbidden to be creative works like a mechanical device, so her essential tool is that device

explanation.surface: A dressmaker forbidden from being creative needs one indispensable tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A sempstress is an old word for a seamstress; one who works without imagination works like a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The motor-driven stitching device is a seamstress's essential tool.

clue.text: Two pairs of braces

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so two pairs of braces is four pairs, a group of eight

explanation.surface: Someone buys two sets of trouser suspenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Braces here are not trouser suspenders (in Britain, what Americans call suspenders) but 'brace' meaning two, as in a brace of pheasants: two pairs of braces is eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Four braces of two make a set of eight, like a group of eight musicians.

clue.text: It means starting out to go to a Yorkshire river

parts.note: to depart is to go
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A traveller explains a trip setting off towards a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaving is the act of setting off on a journey.

clue.text: Puts an object in a hallowed spot

definitions.text: Puts an object in a hallowed spot

parts.words: Puts an object in a hallowed spot
parts.note: placing a relic or treasure in a sacred casket or shrine

explanation.surface: Someone lays an item in a sacred place.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a relic in a sacred casket or holy place is to cherish it there.

clue.text: Oil rich territory I take a pal round?

indicators.note: turning round means the whole run of words is read backwards

parts.note: bud is a friendly word for a pal

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to show a friend round a wealthy Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns I, A and BUD as one run backwards; 'take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf emirate grew rich on petroleum.

clue.text: Regressive period in old fashioned Texan frontier town

indicators.note: in places the turned period inside the rearranged letters
fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters of old are rearranged
regressive means going backwards, so the word for the period is written back to front

parts.note: an era is a period

explanation.surface: Looking back to bygone days in a quaint Wild West town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old fashioned' reads as quaint, but 'fashioned' is the anagram signal on 'old'. Laredo sits on the Rio Grande on the Mexican border.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a Texas city on the Rio Grande, famous from cowboy ballads.

clue.text: Risky game in which players keep their eyes on the ball

definitions.text: Risky game in which players keep their eyes on the ball

parts.words: Risky game in which players keep their eyes on the ball
parts.note: a gambling game where everyone watches a small ball spinning on a wheel

explanation.surface: A dangerous sport where everyone must watch the ball closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests cricket or football; it is a casino wheel game where gamblers watch the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino wheel game is a gamble decided by where a little ball lands.

clue.text: Making a frank impression by coming down with a heavy tread

definitions.text: coming down with a heavy tread

explanation.surface: An honest person makes their mark by walking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: To frank a letter is to mark it with postage, so a frank impression is a postmark made by stamping.
explanation.definitionFit: Franking a letter is marking it with a postage impression, and treading heavily is bringing the feet down hard.

clue.text: Man of unlimited power whose words are recorded

explanation.surface: An all-powerful ruler whose speeches are all taken down.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler is a tyrant, and one who speaks letters aloud to a secretary has their words taken down.

clue.text: Nice tour arranged for those who are hypersensitive

definitions.note: the answer is used here as a noun for such people, so it stands for one of them

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of nice tour are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip to the Riviera city has been organised for highly strung travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective but is the French city, here only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious and overly sensitive is often called this in everyday speech.

clue.text: Inverted maxim on an empire that has vanished

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the word for maxim upwards

parts.note: a motto is a maxim

explanation.surface: A saying turned on its head about an empire now gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inverted' turns MOTTO into OTTOM; 'on' is a link in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish empire ruled from Constantinople until it was dissolved in 1922.

clue.text: Baffling problem I tease Megan about

indicators.note: to tease is to pull apart, so the letters are pulled about
about means the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A puzzle that someone uses to tease their friend Megan.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling riddle or mystery is hard to solve.

clue.text: It serves as a breathing space

definitions.text: It serves as a breathing space

parts.words: It serves as a breathing space
parts.note: a breathing space is usually a rest, but here it is a literal opening through which air is drawn

explanation.surface: Something provides a short break or pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathing space' suggests a pause; here it is an opening you breathe through.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is a channel for air.

clue.text: Loudly lamented doctor coming to a bad end?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: bad means the letters of the word end are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A medic complains bitterly about an unhappy ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges END into NED; 'coming to' is a link, and the question mark marks the playful surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament loudly is to wail or groan in sorrow.

clue.text: A sharp ambassador having a whip-round?

indicators.note: round means the whip goes around the ambassador

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
HE stands for His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy organising a collection among colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection; split it into a whip going round. A sharp is old slang for a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, or sharper, is a swindler who tricks people at cards.

clue.text: Wild oats I ascribe to every leading Irish politician

indicators.note: wild means the letters of oats I are scattered into a new order

parts.note: each means every

explanation.surface: Someone attributes youthful indiscretions to every top Irish leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild oats' looks like a phrase; 'Wild' rearranges OATS I into TAOIS. The Taoiseach is the Irish prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish prime minister is the head of the government in Dublin.

clue.text: Said to indicate across the Channel

definitions.text: Said to indicate across the Channel

parts.words: Said to indicate across the Channel
parts.note: the word said in France when parting from someone

explanation.surface: Something spoken to point out the other side of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Across the Channel means in France; the clue may be misprinted in this old printing.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell means goodbye.

clue.text: A pulpy fruit swallowed by a French robot

indicators.note: swallowed by means the fruit goes inside the French word

parts.note: un is French for a
a tomato is a pulpy fruit

explanation.surface: A French robot eats a soft fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that moves by itself, a mechanical figure.

clue.text: Give a ruling about doctored gin

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so the letters of gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge delivers a verdict concerning spiked spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch.

clue.text: Unwilling to accept the account?

parts.note: refusing to believe a story; account also suggests a bank, hinting at credit

explanation.surface: A customer refuses to accept a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account' suggests a bill or bank; it means a story told, and the answer contains 'credulous', hinting at credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelieving and sceptical describe someone who doubts what they are told.
